title: Preparation of the Fwd Lower Shell Skin Panel for a Structural Repair
abstract: Preparation of the forward lower shell skin panel for a structural repair: damage mapping, material removal to a smooth boundary and the dye penetrant check of the routed edge.

sections.purpose: This task gives the preparation steps that must be done on the forward lower shell skin panel before any repair scheme is applied, up to and including the dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge.
sections.job_setup_note: Map the damage and its position relative to the nearest frame station and stringer before any material is removed, because the repair layout depends on it and the reference is lost once the routing starts. Protect the compartment below the work area from swarf. The dye penetrant inspection at the end must be done by a qualified operator; a routed edge that has not been penetrant checked is not acceptable for any repair scheme.
sections.procedure: 1. Get access to the panel from inside the compartment in zone 116 and from outside on a platform. 2. Clean the damaged area and an area of at least 300 mm around it. 3. Map the damage and record its position relative to the nearest frame station and stringer. 4. Do an eddy current inspection to establish the full extent of the damage. 5. Mask the area and protect the compartment below from swarf. WARNING: PUT THE SWARF PROTECTION IN POSITION BEFORE YOU START TO ROUTE. SWARF IN THE LOWER SHELL DRAIN PATH CAN BLOCK IT AND CAUSE CORROSION. 6. Remove the damaged material by routing to a smooth oval with a corner radius of not less than 12 mm. CAUTION: DO NOT LET THE ROUTED BOUNDARY COME CLOSER THAN 15 MM TO A FASTENER CENTRE. THE REPAIR SCHEME IS NOT VALID IF IT DOES. 7. Blend the routed edge and remove all sharp corners. 8. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge. 9. Do a general visual inspection of the stiffener CIN650686-39 and of the lower fitting D5321120273903 behind the panel. 10. Remove the masking and the swarf protection and clean the area.
sections.close_out: Record the damage map, the routed boundary dimensions and the dye penetrant result on the aircraft work card. Apply the temporary protective treatment to the routed edge if the repair is not to be applied in the same shift. Confirm that the drain path in the lower shell is clear before the compartment is closed.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The routed boundary limits in step 6 apply to every repair scheme on this panel unless the scheme states otherwise.

safety_precautions: Put the swarf protection in position before routing.
Use eye protection and local extraction during routing.
Do not release the aircraft with an unprotected routed edge.
